findings.evidence: PBW :59 `abbrev pbwFiltration`, :63 `abbrev pbwFiltrationPrevious`, :171 `instance : IsRingFiltration (pbwFiltration R L) (pbwFiltrationPrevious R L)`; Clifford :105 `def filtration`, :110 `def filtrationPrevious`; Mathlib/RingTheory/FilteredAlgebra/Basic.lean:74 `class IsRingFiltration (F : ι → σ) (F_lt : outParam <| ι → σ) : Prop extends IsFiltration F F_lt, SetLike.GradedMonoid F`.
findings.fix: Make both `def` (unexposed), matching `CliffordAlgebra.filtration`/`filtrationPrevious` at Filtration.lean:105,110, so the PBW names are the canonical opaque surface and the restatements plus the instance are no longer duplicates; give the instance an explicit name.
findings.issue: `abbrev pbwFiltration` (and `abbrev pbwFiltrationPrevious`, line 63) exposes the body and is reducible, so every generic lemma applies directly to a `pbwFiltration` goal and the twelve restatements (:67–:133) are a duplicate name for the same statement; the instance at :171 likewise duplicates `wordFiltration.instIsRingFiltration`, which typeclass search already finds through the abbrev (`IsRingFiltration`'s `F_lt` is an `outParam`), and it is anonymous so its name is auto-generated.

findings.evidence: WordFiltration.lean:58,63,91,189 and CliffordAlgebra/Filtration.lean:114,118,178,248 all carry `@[simp]` on the same four statements.
findings.fix: Once these are `def`-backed (see previous finding), mark those four `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: No PBW lemma carries `@[simp]`, while the corresponding generic and Clifford lemmas all do; `pbwFiltration_zero` (:91), `pbwFiltration_one` (:131), `pbwFiltrationPrevious_zero` (:67) and `pbwFiltrationPrevious_succ` (:71) are the normal-form computations of the first steps.

findings.evidence: WordFiltration.lean:104 `one_mem_wordFiltration`, :146 `wordFiltration_pow`; CliffordAlgebra/Filtration.lean:183 `one_mem_filtration`, :221 `filtration_pow`; no `one_mem_pbwFiltration`/`pbwFiltration_pow` in the new file.
findings.issue: The PBW restatement set is incomplete relative to the generic API it specializes: no `one_mem_pbwFiltration` and no `pbwFiltration_pow`, although the PR description advertises "powers" and both exist generically and for Clifford. Under an opaque `def` these become genuinely unavailable to consumers.

findings.evidence: Line 30: "`pbwFiltration`: words of length at most `k` in `ι(R)`"; definition at :59–60 uses `LieHom.toLinearMap (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι R)` applied to elements of `L`.
findings.fix: Write "words of length at most `k` in the image of `UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι R : L →ₗ⁅R⁆ U(L)`".
findings.issue: Module-doc summary of the main definition says words "in `ι(R)`", which names the image of the base ring rather than the generator set; the generators are `ι R x` for `x : L`, i.e. `LinearMap.range (ι R).toLinearMap`.

summary: The PBW layer is declared with `abbrev`, which exposes the body and makes its entire specialized API (and its `IsRingFiltration` instance) reducibly redundant with the generic `wordFiltration` surface; it also carries no `@[simp]` annotations, unlike both the generic file and the Clifford file it was factored from.
